summary: No candidate. Differential EVM-versus-C++ runs found no disagreement. Setup: the released Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 CartesiStateTransition (bytecode from work/dave/released/prt/contracts/out, compiled with the regenerated-patched step; machine/step/src checked byte-identical to work/solidity-step/regenerated-patched/src). It was deployed on a private anvil (port 8619, prague, standard 24 KiB code-size limit and 30M block gas limit, since stopped) and called as transitionState(machineState, counter, proofs, provider). The provider is a harness HashProvider whose root computation copies DaveConsensus.provideMerkleRootOfInput (LibKeccak256.hashBytes, ceilLog2 max LOG2_LEAF, LibBinaryMerkleTree.merkleRoot from cartesi-rollups-contracts alpha.10), with InputBox.getInputHash replaced by a stored hash. In the final runs, all 370 honest transitions (all three forms) were accepted by both the EVM and the C++ verifiers (cartesi.machine:verify_send_cmio_response/verify_step_uarch/verify_reset_uarch) with exactly the expected canonical after-hash: the machine's root hash, or the revert root hash at a rejecting reset. In each case the recipe encoder prt-ethereum.transition_proof produced the same bytes as the driver's own encoder. None of the 8,050 proof mutants was accepted by the EVM or by the C++ analog, and no accept/reject or after-hash disagreement appeared. Largest gas (eth_estimateGas, which includes intrinsic and calldata cost): 4,764,810 for delivery+step of a 65,535/65,536-byte input (transitionState calldata 94,180 bytes). For the Linux 65,508-byte EvmAdvance input it was 4,761,298 gas with 94,148 bytes. Both are under the EIP-7825 cap of 2^24 and the 128 KiB txpool limit. Ordinary steps cost at most 0.89M gas (17,444 bytes), resets 0.51M (rejecting reset 507,395).

evidence.scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/DYNEVM/driver.lua (driver), deploy.sh, prov/src/Provider.sol; outputs out-*.txt in the same directory
runs: baremetal (emit-output template; inputs of 1, 31, 32, 33, 101, 1025, 65535 and 65536 bytes; a rejection 'R' followed by deliveries from the revert state; an exception yield 'E' followed by a no-op delivery; an empty slot past the inputs): 156 honest, 3,476 mutants. The one 'failure' was a harness artifact: a stale provider entry left by an aborted earlier run in the same provider contract made the empty slot look like an input. It went away once the provider was redeployed per workload (halt, linux, boot and synth runs, all with fresh deployments, include clean empty-slot cases).

halt (accept, then 'H' halt, then two no-op deliveries to the halted machine, fixed-point steps and resets): 41 honest, 889 mutants (plus two earlier exploratory runs: 61/1,418 and 47/1,082; the latter's two 'failures' were driver bugs: a step-form case at the input-opening counter)

linux (valid-template echo app via the guest-tools rollup CLI; EvmAdvance payloads of 0, 1, 31, 200, 4000 and 65,216 bytes, encoded 292 to 65,508 bytes; a 'reject' payload and the first input after it; random mid-input mcycles with steps at uarch cycles 0, 1-40 and 41-400; the last mcycle; the fixed point after the yield; an empty slot): 134 honest, 2,860 mutants
boot (linux-rootfs from mcycle 0, 7 random mcycles before its halt at 48.6M, steps at 4 uarch cycles each plus step+reset): 35 honest, 735 mutants

synth (unreachable, written through the API: mcycle 2^64-2^40 so imcyclemax saturates on delivery; uarch_cycle = UMAX and UMAX-1 for the cycle-overflow no-op and the overflow after one instruction): 4 honest, 90 mutants
evidence.mutation_classes: One random bit flip in the first chunk of 3 random accesses plus 2-3 random chunks per case, plus the last chunk. Each flip goes into a leaf/read word (the C++ analog recomputes read_hash and the written leaf), a write's old drive hash, a revert-root preimage or a sibling hash. Also: truncation by 1, 8, 31 and 32 bytes; the last access dropped; 1, 32-zero and 32-random trailing bytes; the last access duplicated; the whole body duplicated; 3 swaps of adjacent differing chunks (the C++ analog swaps siblings); a flipped before-hash; the step proof at the reset counter and the reset proof at a step counter. At input openings also: length prefix +1, -1, 0, +32, 2^32-1 and 2^63; one input byte flipped; 32 bytes smuggled into an empty slot (InputBytesWithoutInput).
evidence.compute: About 16 minutes in total, single driver process, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 for the later runs, on a machine with load average around 20

not_covered: Uarch steps that execute the write-TLB ecall: two scans of about 90k logged uarch steps on the Linux boot found no write into the shadow-TLB range (0x1000-0x7000), and a scan of the echo-app input was killed at its 300 s timeout, so no TLB-write step went through the EVM in this round (earlier rounds sampled TLB-flush mcycles)

The full Tournament.winLeafMatch transaction and the real DaveConsensus/InputBox provider: CartesiStateTransition was called directly with a provider that copies DaveConsensus' root computation, so Tournament overhead and the refund modifier were not measured
Inputs between 64 KiB and the 2 MiB rx buffer and larger than the rx buffer (the oversized no-op): not reachable through InputBox; not run on the EVM
imcyclemax reached by execution (2^48 mcycles); only the saturating arithmetic of the delivery was checked, on a synthetic state
A uarch that does not halt before uarch cycle 2^20-1 in a reachable mcycle; only the synthetic cycle-overflow states were checked

Mutation coverage is sampled: not every 32-byte chunk of every proof was flipped, and multi-chunk consistent rewrites (for example a recomputed alternative Merkle path) were not attempted. They would require a hash collision.
The SHA-256 hash-function variant: the EVM step is Keccak only
No ASan/UBSan run of the C++ verifiers on the mutants: the plain build was used (earlier rounds fuzzed the C++ verifiers under the sanitizer)
Dave contracts built with other compiler settings (only the released via-IR build was deployed)
